name: Pahath-moab
overview: Pahath-moab was a male figure noted primarily for his descendants who returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity, indicating his family's role in the restoration period. Though his tribal affiliation is not explicitly recorded, he is mentioned among those who sealed a covenant in Nehemiah 10:14. His presence in these records highlights his family's involvement in the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Pahath-moab means 'supervisor of Moab,' which is a proper name not given directly by God. This title suggests a leadership or administrative role connected to the Moab region, as indicated in Ezra 2:6.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Pahath-moab was a descendant of Jacob, linking him to the broader Israelite lineage. Additionally, several ancestors are associated with him, including Zerahiah, Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, Manasseh, Hasshub, Joab, and Jeshua, reflecting a rich genealogical background documented in Ezra and Nehemiah.
scriptureSignificance: Pahath-moab's significance lies in his family's return to Judah following the exile, marking them as part of the faithful remnant who contributed to the rebuilding of Jerusalem and the reestablishment of the covenant community. His name's appearance on the sealed document in Nehemiah underscores his family's commitment to the covenant renewal and the restoration efforts under Nehemiah's leadership.
